summary:
Red team of the extraction of Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen, A local model for the trianguline variety and applications (Publ. Math. IHÉS 130 (2019) 299–412; arXiv:1702.02192v1). Both recorded artifacts were re-downloaded, and their hashes match. The whole published text was re-read by section groups, and every finding was re-checked personally, four pages on rendered images. There are 20 findings: 4 high, 7 medium, 9 low.

The item statements are mostly faithful, and E2–E7, E9–E11 are real. The weak points are the 12 'planned' statuses, which the review checked only for existence of the named layer, and a mathematical error in §4.3 that nobody recorded.

High:
(1) Category O, Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials, the Kazhdan–Lusztig multiplicity theorem and the D-module input of §2.4 have no owner. Item 2.4-category-O is 'planned' at Tau Ceti LieHighestWeight Layer 3, which explicitly excludes category O, and route 1's brief tells the design job to import them from Tau Ceti.
(2) The trianguline variety itself (item 3.7-xtri) is 'planned' at LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3, i.e. Kisin's potentially semistable rings. This contradicts route 2's own reason, and the Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao input it needs (PG.7) is not upstream of R08.3.
(3) B_dR-representations, almost de Rham theory, Fontaine's equivalence and Berger's W_dR are 'planned' at PadicHodgeTheory P7, whose text and 60-node packet plan none of them. Route 2's brief constructs them at the same time. The accepted Fargues–Fontaine routing puts B_dR-representations and B-pairs in the PadicHodgeTheory Part II.
(4) Theorem 1.9, Conjecture 4.3.4, Remark 4.3.5, (4.12) and Theorem 4.3.8 give the character-fibre cycles codimension [K:Q_p]n(n+3)/2. The paper's own dimensions give [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2 + n. For n = 1 and [K:Q_p] = 2 the printed codimension exceeds the dimension of the ring. The error is not recorded, and five items copy it.

Medium:
- (5) Completed cohomology is sent to R31.2 instead of CompletedCohomologyPartII.
- (6) The CEGGPS patched module and the patched eigenvariety are 'planned' at R31.5, which plans neither; another accepted extraction records the CEGGPS module as missing.
- (7) The definite-unitary eigenvariety is already planned at AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.3 and PadicFamilies L2a.
- (8) The Orlik–Strauch and Emerton Jacquet theory has no items, and route 3's brief duplicates LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (PAPER-DING-25).
- (9) The algebraic flag-variety setting is 'planned' at the complex Lie-groups layer.
- (10) Lemma 2.3.2 (miracle flatness) is false as stated, and item 2.3.2 copies it.
- (11) E8's correction ('free over A⊗K') is itself wrong for τ-dependent weights.

Low:
- (12) Bruhat order, w₀, the dot action, Verma modules and B_dR are in the pinned libraries, although the extraction and the review say nothing is.
- (13) E1 is mis-classified as a new misprint, and the preprint's missing hypothesis ᵖ√1 ∉ F is unrecorded.
- (14) Five item notes cite the wrong E-number, and the review misattributes the extractor.
- (15) Three routing slips.
- (16) PG.7 only partly plans the t-inverted (φ,Γ) theory.
- (17) The Part II parent ('over Q', GL₂) is a poor fit, and make_queue merges it with unrelated Part IIs.
- (18) Two proof gaps (Propositions 2.3.3 and 3.7.2).
- (19) Four unrecorded slips.
- (20) Six unfaithful items.

No cycles. The review changed nothing, so it introduced no error. Disclosure: this session reviewed PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18 (PR #4683), on whose route 5 finding 3 relies.
checked: Independence. PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 was written by Claude Code session cc-fb70e5 (issue #1456, PR #2022; provenance line of the .md and research/errata/REGISTER.md). REV-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 was written by Claude Code session cc-d67081 (issue #1457, PR #2464; review.json verification block and the review report). The review names the extractor as cc-442dc5, which contradicts the extraction's own provenance line (finding 14). The string cc-f805bf occurs in none of the four target files, and git log shows no commit by this session on them.

Disclosure. This session reviewed PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18 (PR #4683), whose route 5 sends B_dR-representations and B-pairs to the PadicHodgeTheory Part II and 'exports B-pairs … to TriangulineVarietyAndItsLocalModel, which currently expects them from P7'. Finding 3 relies on that route and says so. This session also wrote PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20; no finding touches it.

Sources. Published Numdam PDF https://www.numdam.org/item/10.1007/s10240-019-00111-y.pdf re-downloaded on 30 September 2026. It has 114 pages, printed page = PDF page + 298, and sha256 34ffd697…6993967a, matching the record. arXiv:1702.02192: the arXiv API lists only v1 (7 February 2017); it was re-downloaded and its sha256 4c967337…dbcf961 matches the record. The authors' copy on Schraen's page (BHS3.pdf, 1 July 2019, 92 pp.) was read for the codimension formula. Errata: Crossref lists no update-to, updated-by or relation for the DOI. A web search and Schraen's page found no erratum for this paper; the erratum listed there is for the GL₃ paper.

Reading. Three parallel readers read the whole published text by section groups: §§1–2 (pp. 299–328), §3 (pp. 329–371) and §§4–5 with the references (pp. 371–412). Each compared every item in range for statement, hypotheses and locator, checked the recorded sourceIssues in range, and listed uncovered numbered statements and unrecorded slips. I personally re-checked every finding filed here in the text layer. Four pages were rendered and read as images: p. 305 (Theorem 1.9), p. 323 (E6: the printed relation is 'P_{w,w′}(1) = 0 unless w′ ≼ w', so E6 stands), p. 381 (Conjecture 4.3.4, Remark 4.3.5) and p. 405 (Step 10). I checked the dimension count behind finding 4 against pp. 365, 377, 379 and 382 and Lemma 3.5.5. I verified the counterexample in finding 10 directly.

Coverage. Every numbered Theorem, Proposition, Corollary, Lemma, Definition, Conjecture and Remark of §§1–5 has an item, except the following. Remarks 3.3.1, 4.1.2 and 4.2.2 and Lemma 4.3.3 are proof-level. The notation block of pp. 308–309 (ε, unr, excellent-ring facts) and B_pHT/D_pHT are also uncovered, and none of these was judged worth a finding. The objects of the brief were all checked: trianguline (φ,Γ)-modules over the Robba ring (items 3.3-*), X_tri (3.7-xtri, finding 2), Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao (3.7.1, 3.7.3, route 7), B-pairs (inside 3.5.1, finding 3), almost de Rham representations (3.1-*, finding 3), the Grothendieck–Springer resolution and X_w (2.1–2.3, routes 1 and 8), the Steinberg variety and characteristic cycles (2.4–2.5, finding 1), category O and Kazhdan–Lusztig theory (finding 1), companion points and the socle conjecture (4.2.x, 5.3.x), patched eigenvarieties and Taylor–Wiles patching (5.1-patched, finding 6), Emerton's Jacquet functor (finding 8), classicality (5.1.3), smoothness, unibranchness, Cohen–Macaulayness and normality of X_w (2.3.3, 2.3.6, 3.7.10). The source says nothing about generalized Steinberg or Bezrukavnikov beyond Bezrukavnikov–Riche's Cohen–Macaulayness, which item 2.3.3 records. The exact hypotheses p > 2, F/Q_p finite, crystalline generic and regular weights were checked in items 1-taylor-wiles, 5.1-setting, 3.7.9, 4.2.3, 4.3.8, 5.1.3, 5.3.3 and 5.4.2. They are faithful, apart from item 5.4.1 (finding 20).

Statuses. I read every planned layer at its atlas text in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/*.json, and its accepted packet where one exists, and asked whether it plans the item in the paper's generality: tauceti LieGroups Layer 8 (finding 9), LieHighestWeight Layers 3, 6 and 7 (finding 1), PadicHodgeTheory P7 with its 60-node packet (finding 3), PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.3 and PG.7 with their packet and README (finding 16), PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.0, LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1 and R08.3 with their packet nodes (finding 2), and CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.2 and R31.5 (findings 5, 6). I also read the would-be owners CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.0–CC.8, AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.3, PadicFamilies L2, L2a and L3, OverconvergentAutomorphicForms O0 and O6, LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0, L1 and L4, PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0a, tauceti ReductiveGroups Layers 6–7, ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2 and RG2.4, and tauceti RootSystems Layer 3. No research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json, packet or README exists yet for SpringerResolutionAndCharacteristicCycles, TriangulineVarietyAndItsLocalModel or the CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility Part II; their DESIGN jobs are pending in research/blueprint/queue.json, so there was no accepted design to compare against.

Library. I searched declarations.tsv at the pinned baseline (Mathlib 082e2d3, Tau Ceti f790474) for Bruhat, Kazhdan–Lusztig, Iwahori–Hecke, Verma, category O, BGG, Springer, Steinberg, flag variety, Schubert, almost de Rham, B_dR, Robba, trianguline, (φ,Γ), Hodge–Tate, de Rham, eigenvariety, D-module, holonomic, characteristic cycle, Cohen–Macaulay, miracle flatness, Schlessinger, pro-representability, formally smooth, longest element, dot action and cyclotomic character. I opened and read these files: Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean (BDeRhamPlus :77, BDeRham :90), TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Bruhat.lean (BruhatStep :84, BruhatLE :156, bruhatPartialOrder :240), TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/HighestWeight/Verma.lean (VermaModule :196, irreducibleQuotient :416), TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/Weyl/DotAction.lean (dotAction :108) and TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/LongestElement.lean (longestElement :194). Nothing in either library covers the Robba ring, (φ,Γ)-modules, almost de Rham theory, category O, Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials, D-modules, Cohen–Macaulay rings or eigenvarieties. So all 'missing' statuses other than those in findings 1–3, 5–9 and 12 are correct.

Routes, order and cycles. I computed the ancestor set of every routed stage (P7, PG.3, PG.7, RD.0, R08.1, R08.3, R31.2, R31.5) from data/atlas.json stage requirements, parent stages and stageEdges, plus every link in research/blueprint/restructure, packets and links (4,642 extra links). Including unaccepted links can only add ancestors, so 'not upstream' claims are conservative. No routed stage has CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility or either new roadmap among its ancestors. The planned import graph, TriangulineVariety → {P7, PG, RD.0, R08, SpringerResolution} with the Part II depending on the parent and on TriangulineVariety, is therefore acyclic. Order problems: R08.3 lacks PG.7 upstream (finding 2), and R31.5 lacks any trianguline or Jacquet stage (finding 6). Other extractions compared: PAPER-DING-25 (routes 1–11), PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21 (routes 4–5), PAPER-DOSPINESCU-LEBRAS-17 (route 4), PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18 (route 5), PAPER-BOCKLE-IYENGAR-PASKUNAS-23 (route 7), PAPER-PAN-26 (route 1, item 540), PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15 (B-pair items) and PAPER-NAKAMURA-23. There are no extractions of Breuil–Ding, of the earlier BHS papers [19] and [20], or of Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao. I also read research/blueprint/make_queue.py on how Part II proposals merge (finding 17).

Source issues. E1–E11 were re-checked at their locators. E2, E3, E4, E5, E6 (on a page image), E7, E9, E10 and E11 are real as printed. E8 is real, but its correction is wrong (finding 11). E1 is mis-classified, and so are the kinds of E2 and E3 (finding 13). Unrecorded mistakes filed: the character-fibre codimension (finding 4), the false miracle-flatness lemma (finding 10), two proof gaps (finding 18) and four slips (finding 19). Reported by readers but not filed: p. 324 'T*(G/B × G/B) ≃ g̃ × g̃', where Ñ × Ñ is meant, because it turns on a glyph I did not render; the [16, Conj. 6.5] versus [16, Conj. 6.6] citation, because [16] was not read; the non-negativity of a_{w,w′} in Theorem 2.4.7(iii), which is true since characteristic cycles are effective, so only the proof is terse; and the 'n ≤ 7' clause of Remark 2.4.5, not checked against [47].

The review. It changed nothing, so it introduced no error into the extraction. Its report states three things this red team contradicts: 'No library items, which is correct: nothing in this paper is in the pinned libraries' (finding 12); that the planned items were checked only in that they 'nam[e] atlas layers that exist', not for content (findings 1–3, 5, 6, 9); and the extractor's session (finding 14). It confirmed E8's correction, which is wrong (finding 11), and E1's 'known: new' (finding 13).

findings.claim: Item 2.4-category-O is marked planned at Tau Ceti LieHighestWeight Layer 3, and route 1's brief tells the design job to 'Import category O, Verma modules and Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials from the Tau Ceti representation-theory roadmaps rather than rebuilding them'. The Tau Ceti roadmap plans Verma modules and L(λ) only, and says explicitly that category O and the linkage principle are a separate development it does not plan. The item's statement goes far beyond Verma modules. It includes (a) the BGG category O and its block O(0) of trivial infinitesimal character; (b) the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials P_{x,y}, with P_{x,y} ≠ 0 iff x ≼ y and P_{x,x}(1) = 1; and (c) the multiplicity formula [M(ww₀·0) : L(w′w₀·0)] = P_{w₀w,w₀w′}(1). Item (c) is the Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture, proved by Beilinson–Bernstein and Brylinski–Kashiwara, which the paper cites through Humphreys §8.4. That theorem is what Theorem 2.4.7(ii), Corollary 2.5.6, Corollary 4.3.2 (4.9), Theorem 4.3.8 and the cycle identities (1.2)–(1.3) and (5.23)–(5.24) rest on. No atlas stage plans category O, Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials, the Kazhdan–Lusztig theorem or D-modules: a text search of every stage of research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps finds 0 hits for 'category O' and 'D-module', and 'Kazhdan' only in EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.6 (Kazhdan–Varshavsky transfer). The D-module input of §2.4 is also used but not itemised: coherent D-modules on a smooth variety, good filtrations, the characteristic variety and cycle ([44, Cor. 2.3.2]), holonomic and regular holonomic G-equivariant D-modules, and the Beilinson–Bernstein localisation theorem on G/B. So the design job would import a theory that nothing plans, and the central multiplicity theorem has no owner. The same wrong assumption occurs in the accepted PAPER-DING-25 route 1 brief ('import category O, Verma modules and their composition factors from the Tau Ceti Lie highest weight roadmap').
findings.evidence: Paper p. 320: 'Let us denote by O the usual BGG-category of U(g)-modules … the constituent L(w′w₀·0) occurs in M(ww₀·0) with multiplicity P_{w₀w,w₀w′}(1), see e.g. [45, §8.4]. Here P_{x,y}(T) ∈ Z_{≥0}[T] is the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial'; p. 321: 'We write O(0) for the full subcategory of O consisting of objects of trivial infinitesimal character … The Beilinson-Bernstein correspondence [1, 21] defines an exact functor which is an equivalence of artinian categories … to the category D−Mod^rh_{G/B×G/B} of regular holonomic G-equivariant D-modules'; p. 321: 'To any coherent D-module M on G/B × G/B one can associate a coherent O_{T*(G/B×G/B)}-module gr(M) … (which depends on the choice of a good filtration on M)'. research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_RepresentationTheory_LieHighestWeight.json, Layer 6: 'Do **not** invoke a full BGG resolution or category `O`; those are a separate development and are not assumed here'; Layer 7: 'The full **linkage principle** of category `O` (the precise statement about composition factors of `M(λ)`, the integral Weyl group, and the order constraints of the block decomposition) is strictly stronger and is a separate development, not identified with this orbit statement.' Layer 3 plans PBW, Verma modules, the Kostant partition function and L(λ) only. At the pinned Tau Ceti commit f790474 no declaration name contains KazhdanLusztig, IwahoriHecke, CategoryO or Holonomic (declarations.tsv).

findings.claim: Item 3.7-xtri defines the trianguline variety X_tri(r̄). It is the Zariski closure of U_tri(r̄) in 𝔛_r̄ × T^n_L, with T_reg and T^n_reg, and it records that X_tri(r̄) is reduced and equidimensional of dimension n² + [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2 with U_tri open ([19, Th. 2.6]). The item is marked planned at LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.3, but R08.3 plans Kisin's potentially semistable deformation rings of fixed Hodge and inertial type and says nothing of trianguline representations, characters of K^× or Zariski closures. Route 2's own reason says the opposite: 'The trianguline variety is not planned anywhere in the atlas … never as the geometric object X_tri(r̄)'. Route 2's brief never asks for the construction of X_tri(r̄), and route 5 sends the item to R08.3 as a source. So the paper's central object has no owner. The placement also cannot work in the atlas order. Defining U_tri needs trianguline (φ,Γ_K)-modules and parameters, and the proofs of Propositions 3.7.1–3.7.2 need Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao's global triangulation ([49, Cor. 6.3.10, Th. 6.3.13]), which is owned by PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology:PG.7. PG.7 is not among the 202 ancestors of R08.3, computed from data/atlas.json stage requirements and stage edges plus every packet, restructure and link-file link. Item 3.6-galois-groupoids has a smaller problem of the same kind. Only its first clause (the framed deformation groupoid X_r, and X_r → X_V formally smooth of relative dimension n²) is R08.1 material. Its trianguline groupoids X_{V,M•} and X_{r,M•}, their framed versions and the equivalence X_V ≅ X_D induced by D_rig are not planned at R08.1. The accepted PAPER-DING-25 has the same error: its item 4.1-xtri is planned at R08.3.

The paper states the cycles C_{r,Π} of Theorem 1.9 / Conjecture 4.3.4 / Theorem 4.3.8, and the cycles 𝒵_{w′}, 𝒞_{w′} of (4.12), with codimension [K:Q_p]·n(n+3)/2 in Spec Ô_{𝔛_r̄,r}. Remark 4.3.5 correspondingly says the character fibre has dimension n² + [K:Q_p]·n(n−3)/2. Both are wrong whenever d := [K:Q_p] > 1. The correct values are codimension d·n(n+1)/2 + n and fibre dimension n² − n + d·n(n−1)/2. Five items copy the wrong number, as do the extraction's conventions and gaps, and it is not recorded as a source issue.

The argument uses only the paper's own dimensions.
- Spec Ô_{𝔛_r̄,r} is equidimensional of dimension n² + dn² (p. 377).
- The weight fibre Spec R_{r,M•} has codimension d·n(n+1)/2, i.e. dimension n² + d·n(n−1)/2 (p. 379). This is correct: X_tri has dimension n² + d·n(n+1)/2 and the weight space 𝒲^n has dimension dn.
- The diagram (4.11) is obtained from (4.6) by 'taking the fibers over δ ∈ Spec Ô_{T^n_{L,wt(δ)},δ}' (p. 382). Here T^n_{L,wt(δ)} is the fibre of wt : T^n_L → t^rig, which has dimension n. The character space T of K^× has dimension d + 1 (a G_m for the uniformiser times the weight space of O_K^×), and Lemma 3.5.5 says wt − wt(δ) : T̂^n_δ → t̂ is formally smooth of relative dimension n.
- By flatness (Proposition 4.1.1), this cuts n further dimensions, giving codimension d·n(n+1)/2 + n. The printed d·n(n+3)/2 = d·n(n+1)/2 + dn cuts dn.

A check: n = 1, d = 2. Spec Ô_{𝔛_r̄,r} has dimension 3, and the fibre over δ is a point, of codimension 3 = d·1·2/2 + 1. The printed value is 4, which exceeds the dimension of the ring, and Remark 4.3.5 gives the fibre dimension 1 + 2·(−2)/2 = −1. For K = Q_p the two formulas agree, which is why the GL₂(Q_p) example on p. 305 ('two irreducible components of dimension 3') is consistent. §5 is unaffected, since it uses only weight fibres, with d = [F⁺:Q]n(n+1)/2 on p. 399.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19.result.json: item PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19/2.3.2-miracle-flatness; sourceIssues (not recorded)
findings.claim: Item 2.3.2 copies Lemma 2.3.2 as printed: 'Let f : Y → Z be a morphism of noetherian schemes with Z regular, Y Cohen–Macaulay and all fibres equidimensional of dimension dim Y − dim Z. Then f is flat.' That statement is false. Take Y = Spec k ⊔ A¹_k → Z = A¹_k, mapping the isolated point to 0 and A¹ by the identity. Z is regular, Y is Cohen–Macaulay of dimension 1, and every fibre is equidimensional of dimension 0 = dim Y − dim Z. But f is not flat at the isolated point, because k[t] → k, t ↦ 0, is not flat. Miracle flatness needs the local equality dim O_{Y,y} = dim O_{Z,f(y)} + dim O_{Y_{f(y)},y} at each point, as in Matsumoto, Theorem 23.1 and EGA IV 6.1.5. The paper's proof uses exactly this local equality ('dim S/(f₁,…,f_d)S = dim S − d'). That equality follows from the global hypothesis when Y is equidimensional of finite type over a field and Z is irreducible. Every use in the paper satisfies this: X_w and V_w are irreducible, and X is equidimensional (Proposition 2.3.3, Lemma 2.3.5). So no result of the paper is affected, but the item, and hence the roadmap node, states a false lemma.
findings.evidence: Published p. 315: 'Lemma 2.3.2. — Let f : Y → Z be a morphism of noetherian schemes and assume that Z is regular and Y is Cohen-Macaulay. Assume that the fibers of f are equidimensional of dimension dim Y − dim Z. Then f is flat.' The counterexample is as stated in the claim.

findings.claim: E8 correctly records that p. 337 requires the graded pieces of a filtered A⊗_{Q_p}K-representation of G_a to be 'free of rank 1 over A⊗_{Q_p}K for i ∈ Z'. But its correction, 'free over A⊗_{Q_p}K', is also wrong, and the review confirmed it without comment. Since L splits K, L⊗_{Q_p}K ≅ ∏_{τ∈Σ} L, and a filtration of V decomposes as ⊕_τ Fil^i_τ. The graded pieces gr^i = ⊕_τ gr^i_τ are free over L⊗K only if dim gr^i_τ is independent of τ. For the rank-one W⁺ = W⁺_dR(R_{L,K}(z^k)) with non-parallel k = (k_τ), the jump of the τ-component is at −k_τ. So gr^{−k_τ} is non-zero only in the τ-slot, and is not free over L⊗K. The paper handles exactly such τ-dependent jumps throughout: (3.9) is 'Fil_{W⁺_A,i} := ⊕_{τ∈Σ} Fil^{−h_{τ,i}}_{W⁺_A}(D_{pdR,τ}(W_A))', and Corollary 3.2.3 works τ by τ. With E8's correction, Lemma 3.2.2 would exclude these objects and its equivalence would fail to be essentially surjective. What the paper uses, and proves on p. 340, is that the τ-components are free A-modules: 'It follows from Lemma 3.2.2 that they are all free A-modules of finite type.' Equivalently each gr^i is a finite projective A⊗_{Q_p}K-module. E8's reason, 'Rank one is imposed later and separately, through regularity', should also go.

findings.claim: Two proof gaps are unrecorded. In each the result is right and the repair is short. (a) Proposition 2.3.3, p. 316. The proof shows that X_{A,w} over A = Z_(p) is Cohen–Macaulay along its special fibre, then concludes by localisation ('It then follows e.g. from [31, Prop. 18.8] that the generic fiber X_{k,w} is Cohen-Macaulay'). That only reaches the generic points whose closure meets the special fibre. X_A is not proper over A (its g-factor is affine), so not every point specialises. The repair: the non-Cohen–Macaulay locus is closed and stable under the G_m-scaling (2.8) of ψ. So if non-empty its closure meets (G/B)²_A × {0}, which is proper over A and hence meets the special fibre. (b) Proposition 3.7.2, pp. 366–367. The proof fixes a single point x̃ of Ũ over x, for a proper birational f : Ũ → U, and asserts that the map of complete local rings Ô_{U,x} → Ô_{Ũ,x̃} is injective ('the left vertical arrow is dominant, i.e. … the induced map on the corresponding complete local rings is injective'). For a single x̃ this fails when U has several branches at x. For example, at the node of a nodal curve with x̃ one point of the normalisation, k[[a,b]]/(ab) → k[[t]] is not injective. Local irreducibility of X_tri at x is proved only later (Corollary 3.7.10), using this proposition. The repair is to use all points of f⁻¹(x). Since Ũ → U is proper and surjective onto each branch, every minimal prime of the reduced ring Ô_{U,x} contains the kernel for some x̃, so the intersection of the kernels is 0. The factorisation through the closed subfunctor X_{r,M•} then follows.
